column5: fact   (ALL DISEASE, THERAPY, CENTER AND ACCOUNT FACTS BELOW ARE FICTIONAL DEMO DATA)

Disease (fictional demo): Hemoryx syndrome, a rare inherited blood-nerve disorder. Roughly 200 diagnosed patients in the territory; average time to diagnosis is about 6 years. Typical presentation is a mix of unexplained anemia, episodic nerve pain and fatigue that individually point to other conditions.

Approved therapy (fictional demo): Vorexa, indicated for adults with confirmed Hemoryx syndrome. Diagnosis must be confirmed by genetic testing at or through an expert center. Product discussion only on the approved label and only if the HCP asks.

Diagnostic journey steps in order: 1 Unexplained signals (anemia, nerve pain, fatigue without a clear cause); 2 Multiple specialist referrals (hematology, neurology, primary care without a unifying diagnosis); 3 Delayed diagnosis (typically years); 4 Referral to expert center (genetic testing); 5 Confirmed and supported (care plan and support program).

Awareness signals that should prompt considering referral for evaluation (clinician judgement only; the rep never applies these to a specific patient): persistent unexplained anemia with normal iron studies; recurrent episodic neuropathic pain; family history of unexplained anemia and neuropathy; two or more specialists consulted without a unifying diagnosis.

Approved disease-awareness materials: HX-101 Disease Overview for hematologists; HX-102 Neurology Recognition Guide for neurologists; HX-103 Primary Care One-Page Signal Checklist for primary care and internal medicine. All must be used as supplied; no edits.

Patient support program (fictional): the HCP or expert center submits an enrollment form; patient consent is obtained by the HCP, not the rep. The rep may share the program information sheet but may not collect patient information or complete forms for the HCP. Genetic testing sponsorship is arranged through the expert center.

Questions about whether a patient's symptoms indicate the disease, any diagnostic or off-label question, and any clinical question go to Medical Information (1-800-000-0200, fictional). Possible adverse events must be reported per SOP within 24 hours. Reps never discuss individual patients.

Demo expert center for Hemoryx syndrome in the Bay Area: multidisciplinary clinic, genetic testing available, accepts referrals from community hematologists and neurologists, new-patient wait about 3 weeks.
Demo expert center for the Southeast: multidisciplinary clinic, genetic testing available, accepts referrals, new-patient wait about 5 weeks.

Demo note: community hematologist in San Francisco. Has never treated or referred a Hemoryx patient. Received the HX-101 overview once; neutral reaction, said he had not heard of the condition. Nearest expert center: El Camino Health.
Demo note: neurologist in Palo Alto. Sees many patients with episodic nerve pain. No disease-awareness material received yet. Nearest expert center: El Camino Health.
Demo note: primary care physician in Mountain View. Received the HX-103 checklist and responded positively; unsure how to refer. Referral route to an expert center not yet confirmed.
